SECTION: Using Your Refrigerator (Pages 9-22)

TOPICS: refrigerator operation, temperature control, component removal and replacement, shelf and bin adjustment, ice maker and dispenser use, cleaning and maintenance, troubleshooting

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- Initial setup requires setting the Refrigerator Control to 3 (range 1-5, with 1 being warmest and 5 coldest) and the Freezer Control to B (range A-C, with A being warmest and C coldest) (Page 9)
- The controls are set correctly when milk/juice is cold and ice cream is firm (Page 9)
- The Automatic Exterior Moisture control does not require adjustment (Page 9)
- When adjusting settings, one should adjust the Refrigerator Control first, wait at least 24 hours, then adjust the Freezer Control if needed (Page 9)
- To remove the drop-in trim piece: Remove all items from the shelf, then pull straight up on the trim piece at each end (Page 10)
- To replace the drop-in trim piece: Locate each end above the trim pocket opening, push down until it stops, then replace items on the shelf (Page 10)
- To remove the snap-on trivet: Remove all items from the shelf, pull out on the inside tab at each end, then lift the trivet straight out (Page 10)
- To replace the snap-on trivet: Line up the ends with the button on the door liner wall, push back until it snaps securely, then replace items on the shelf (Page 10)
- To remove the wine rack: Lift the front of the wine rack, then pull it off the rear-support, and replace in reverse order (Page 10)
- Door bins can be removed by lifting up and pulling straight out; replacement involves sliding in above the support button and pushing down until it stops (Page 11)
- Glass shelves are strong enough to hold bottles, milk, and other heavy food items (Page 11)
- To remove a shelf, items must be removed first, then the shelf is tilted up at the front, lifted at the back, and pulled straight out (Page 11)
- To replace a shelf, rear hooks are guided into slots on the back liner wall, the front is tilted up until hooks drop in, and the front is lowered to a level position (Page 11)
- A note emphasizes that glass shelves are heavy and should be handled carefully (Page 11)
- Instructions for sliding shelves out and in are provided for some models, involving careful pulling or pushing until they stop (Page 11)
- To slide shelf side-to-side: Lift slightly on shelf front, slide to desired location, then lower front to level (Page 12)
- NOTE: Small items do not need to be removed before moving; larger items may need to be removed (Page 12)
- To remove the shelf: Remove all items, hold back of shelf with one hand, lift front to 45° angle, then lower and pull out (Page 12)
- NOTE: Shelf is heavy; use both hands when removing (Page 12)
- To remove shelf track: Lift both sides slightly, then pull track straight out (Page 12)
- To replace shelf track: Guide track hooks into slots on cabinet back wall, ensure hooks are parallel, push track backward and down, and check it is fully seated (Page 12)
- To reinstall a shelf: Hold at front and back, tilt front up to 45°, insert rear slides into upper channel, then lower front to level (Page 13)
- NOTE: Ensure both rear shelf slides are securely in the track before letting go of the shelf (Page 13)
- To remove the crisper: Slide straight out to stop, lift front slightly, then slide out the rest (Page 13)
- To remove the cover (Style 1): Hold firmly, lift front off supports, then pull up and out (Page 13)
- To replace the cover (Style 1): Fit back into notch supports, then lower front into place (Page 13)
- To remove the cover (Style 2): Push up glass insert from bottom, slide out, lift front of frame, then lift frame out (Page 13)
- To replace the cover (Style 2): Fit back of frame into notch supports, then lower front; slide back of glass insert into place, then lower front (Page 13)
- The crisper humidity control can be adjusted between LOW and HIGH settings (Page 14)
- LOW setting allows moist air out for fruits and vegetables with skins; HIGH keeps moist air in for fresh, leafy vegetables (Page 14)
- To remove the meat drawer: slide out to the stop, lift the front slightly, then slide out the rest of the way (Page 14)
- To remove the cover: remove meat drawer and crisper, lift the front of the cover off supports, then pull up and out (Page 14)
- To replace the cover: fit back of cover into notch supports, lower front into place, then replace meat drawer and crisper (Page 14)
- Cold air from the freezer flows into the meat drawer to keep it colder than the rest of the refrigerator (Page 14)
- Slide the control from side to side to let more or less cold air through (Page 14)
- To remove the snack bin: Slide it straight out to the stop, lift the front, slide it out further, and replace in reverse order (Page 15)
- To remove a basket: Slide it out to the stop, lift the front to clear the stop, and slide it out the rest of the way (Page 15)
- To replace a basket: Place it on the slides, ensure wire stops clear the front of the slides, and slide it in all the way (Page 15)
- To remove the freezer shelf: Lift the right side off supports, slide it out of the support holes, and replace in reverse order (Page 15)
- Ice cubes may shrink if not used due to slow evaporation from moving cold air (Page 16)
- To remove ice: hold tray at both ends and twist slightly (Page 16)
- The ON/OFF lever is a wire signal arm; DOWN starts ice making, UP stops it (Page 16)
- Do not turn the ice maker on until it is connected to the water supply (Page 16)
- Softened water can damage the ice maker mold and lead to poor ice quality (Page 16)
- To remove the grille: Open both doors, pull base grille forward to release support tabs, do not remove Tech Sheet (Page 17)
- To replace the grille: Line up grille support tabs with metal clips, push firmly to snap into place, close the doors (Page 17)
- See cleaning instructions for defrost pan and condenser coils on page 22 (Page 17)
- The ice dispenser operates by opening a trapdoor in a chute between the dispenser and the ice bin; a buzzing sound is normal when the door closes (Page 17)
- The dispenser system will not operate when the freezer door is open (Page 17)
- For crushed ice, cubes are crushed before being dispensed, which may cause a slight delay (Page 17)
- When changing from CRUSHED to CUBE, a few ounces of crushed ice will be dispensed along with the first cubes (Page 17)
- Use a sturdy glass when dispensing ice or water to avoid personal injury or breakage (Page 17)
- To dispense ice: Move Ice Selector Switch to CUBE position for cubed ice, or to CRUSHED position for crushed ice (on some models) (Page 17)
- The first few batches of ice may have an off-flavor from new plumbing and parts; throw them away (Page 18)
- Large amounts of ice should be taken from the ice bin, not through the dispenser (Page 18)
- Chilled water comes from a tank behind the meat drawer that holds approximately 1.5 L (1½ quarts) (Page 18)
- When first hooking up the refrigerator, press the water dispenser bar until 1.9 to 2.8 L (2 or 3 quarts) are drawn and discarded to rinse the tank and pipes (Page 18)
- The small tray beneath the dispenser is designed to evaporate small spills; there is no drain in this tray. Do not pour water into it (Page 18)
- To dispense water, press a sturdy glass against the water dispenser bar, then remove the glass to stop dispensing (Page 18)
- Dispense enough water every week to maintain a fresh supply (Page 18)
- To turn on the night light, slide the dispenser LIGHT switch to the left (Page 18)
- A WARNING box states that failure to disconnect power could result in electrical shock or personal injury (Page 20)
- To change the refrigerator light, one must disconnect power, reach behind the Control Console, replace the bulb with a 40-watt appliance bulb, and reconnect power (Page 20)
- To change the crisper light, one must disconnect power, pull the top of the light shield forward, lower it, remove it, replace the bulb, and reassemble (Page 20)
- To change the light below the ice bin, one must disconnect power, push in the sides of the light shield until it snaps free, replace the bulb, and reassemble (Page 20)
- All procedures require a 40-watt appliance bulb (Page 20)
- To change the dispenser area light, disconnect power, remove the bulb, replace it with a heavy-duty 10-watt bulb, then reconnect power (Page 21)
- Not all appliance bulbs will fit; replacement bulbs must be the same size and shape (Page 21)

- To remove the drop-in trim piece: Remove all items from the shelf, then pull straight up on the trim piece at each end (Page 10)
- To replace the drop-in trim piece: Locate each end above the trim pocket opening, push down until it stops, then replace items on the shelf (Page 10)
- To remove the snap-on trivet: Remove all items from the shelf, pull out on the inside tab at each end, then lift the trivet straight out (Page 10)
- To replace the snap-on trivet: Line up the ends with the button on the door liner wall, push back until it snaps securely, then replace items on the shelf (Page 10)
- To remove the wine rack: Lift the front of the wine rack, then pull it off the rear-support, and replace in reverse order (Page 10)
- Door bins can be removed by lifting up and pulling straight out; replacement involves sliding in above the support button and pushing down until it stops (Page 11)
- Glass shelves are strong enough to hold bottles, milk, and other heavy food items (Page 11)
- To remove a shelf, items must be removed first, then the shelf is tilted up at the front, lifted at the back, and pulled straight out (Page 11)
- To replace a shelf, rear hooks are guided into slots on the back liner wall, the front is tilted up until hooks drop in, and the front is lowered to a level position (Page 11)
- A note emphasizes that glass shelves are heavy and should be handled carefully (Page 11)
- Instructions for sliding shelves out and in are provided for some models, involving careful pulling or pushing until they stop (Page 11)
- To slide shelf side-to-side: Lift slightly on shelf front, slide to desired location, then lower front to level (Page 12)
- NOTE: Small items do not need to be removed before moving; larger items may need to be removed (Page 12)
- To remove the shelf: Remove all items, hold back of shelf with one hand, lift front to 45° angle, then lower and pull out (Page 12)
- NOTE: Shelf is heavy; use both hands when removing (Page 12)
- To remove shelf track: Lift both sides slightly, then pull track straight out (Page 12)
- To replace shelf track: Guide track hooks into slots on cabinet back wall, ensure hooks are parallel, push track backward and down, and check it is fully seated (Page 12)
- To reinstall a shelf: Hold at front and back, tilt front up to 45°, insert rear slides into upper channel, then lower front to level (Page 13)
- NOTE: Ensure both rear shelf slides are securely in the track before letting go of the shelf (Page 13)
- To remove the crisper: Slide straight out to stop, lift front slightly, then slide out the rest (Page 13)
- To remove the cover (Style 1): Hold firmly, lift front off supports, then pull up and out (Page 13)
- To replace the cover (Style 1): Fit back into notch supports, then lower front into place (Page 13)
- To remove the cover (Style 2): Push up glass insert from bottom, slide out, lift front of frame, then lift frame out (Page 13)
- To replace the cover (Style 2): Fit back of frame into notch supports, then lower front; slide back of glass insert into place, then lower front (Page 13)
- The crisper humidity control can be adjusted between LOW and HIGH settings (Page 14)
- LOW setting allows moist air out for fruits and vegetables with skins; HIGH keeps moist air in for fresh, leafy vegetables (Page 14)
- To remove the meat drawer: slide out to the stop, lift the front slightly, then slide out the rest of the way (Page 14)
- To remove the cover: remove meat drawer and crisper, lift the front of the cover off supports, then pull up and out (Page 14)
- To replace the cover: fit back of cover into notch supports, lower front into place, then replace meat drawer and crisper (Page 14)
- Cold air from the freezer flows into the meat drawer to keep it colder than the rest of the refrigerator (Page 14)
- Slide the control from side to side to let more or less cold air through (Page 14)
- To remove the snack bin: Slide it straight out to the stop, lift the front, slide it out further, and replace in reverse order (Page 15)
- To remove a basket: Slide it out to the stop, lift the front to clear the stop, and slide it out the rest of the way (Page 15)
- To replace a basket: Place it on the slides, ensure wire stops clear the front of the slides, and slide it in all the way (Page 15)
- To remove the freezer shelf: Lift the right side off supports, slide it out of the support holes, and replace in reverse order (Page 15)
- Ice cubes may shrink if not used due to slow evaporation from moving cold air (Page 16)
- To remove ice: hold tray at both ends and twist slightly (Page 16)
- The ON/OFF lever is a wire signal arm; DOWN starts ice making, UP stops it (Page 16)
- Do not turn the ice maker on until it is connected to the water supply (Page 16)
- Softened water can damage the ice maker mold and lead to poor ice quality (Page 16)
- To remove the grille: Open both doors, pull base grille forward to release support tabs, do not remove Tech Sheet (Page 17)
- To replace the grille: Line up grille support tabs with metal clips, push firmly to snap into place, close the doors (Page 17)
- See cleaning instructions for defrost pan and condenser coils on page 22 (Page 17)
- The ice dispenser operates by opening a trapdoor in a chute between the dispenser and the ice bin; a buzzing sound is normal when the door closes (Page 17)
- The dispenser system will not operate when the freezer door is open (Page 17)
- For crushed ice, cubes are crushed before being dispensed, which may cause a slight delay (Page 17)
- When changing from CRUSHED to CUBE, a few ounces of crushed ice will be dispensed along with the first cubes (Page 17)
- Use a sturdy glass when dispensing ice or water to avoid personal injury or breakage (Page 17)
- To dispense ice: Move Ice Selector Switch to CUBE position for cubed ice, or to CRUSHED position for crushed ice (on some models) (Page 17)
- The first few batches of ice may have an off-flavor from new plumbing and parts; throw them away (Page 18)
- Large amounts of ice should be taken from the ice bin, not through the dispenser (Page 18)
- Chilled water comes from a tank behind the meat drawer that holds approximately 1.5 L (1½ quarts) (Page 18)
- When first hooking up the refrigerator, press the water dispenser bar until 1.9 to 2.8 L (2 or 3 quarts) are drawn and discarded to rinse the tank and pipes (Page 18)
- The small tray beneath the dispenser is designed to evaporate small spills; there is no drain in this tray. Do not pour water into it (Page 18)
- To dispense water, press a sturdy glass against the water dispenser bar, then remove the glass to stop dispensing (Page 18)
- Dispense enough water every week to maintain a fresh supply (Page 18)
- To turn on the night light, slide the dispenser LIGHT switch to the left (Page 18)
- A WARNING box states that failure to disconnect power could result in electrical shock or personal injury (Page 20)
- To change the refrigerator light, one must disconnect power, reach behind the Control Console, replace the bulb with a 40-watt appliance bulb, and reconnect power (Page 20)
- To change the crisper light, one must disconnect power, pull the top of the light shield forward, lower it, remove it, replace the bulb, and reassemble (Page 20)
- To change the light below the ice bin, one must disconnect power, push in the sides of the light shield until it snaps free, replace the bulb, and reassemble (Page 20)
- All procedures require a 40-watt appliance bulb (Page 20)
- To change the dispenser area light, disconnect power, remove the bulb, replace it with a heavy-duty 10-watt bulb, then reconnect power (Page 21)
- Not all appliance bulbs will fit; replacement bulbs must be the same size and shape (Page 21)
- New sounds like slight hum, soft hiss, clicking, water gurgling, and ice maker clatter are normal and caused by fan motors, thermostats, defrost cycles, and water flow (Page 21)
- The refrigerator's high-efficiency compressor runs longer than older models and may seem to run most of the time (Page 21)
- Energy-saving tips include checking door gaskets, cleaning condenser coils, minimizing door openings, and ensuring the refrigerator is not near heat sources (Page 21)
- The refrigerator and freezer sections defrost automatically (Page 22)
- Clean both sections about once a month to prevent odors (Page 22)
- Wipe up spills immediately (Page 22)
- Unplug the refrigerator before cleaning (Page 22)
- A warning states that refrigeration system tubes near the defrost pan can become hot and could cause personal injury if not handled carefully (Page 22)
- The text advises waxing painted metal surfaces at least twice a year for rust protection (Page 22)
- Do not wax plastic parts (Page 22)
- For inside walls, allow the freezer to warm up so the cloth won't stick (Page 22)

- Wipe up spills immediately (Page 22)
- Unplug the refrigerator before cleaning (Page 22)
- A warning states that refrigeration system tubes near the defrost pan can become hot and could cause personal injury if not handled carefully (Page 22)
- Waxing painted metal surfaces at least twice a year for rust protection (Page 22)
- Do not wax plastic parts (Page 22)
- For inside walls, allow the freezer to warm up so the cloth won't stick (Page 22)
- No need to shut off the refrigerator if away for less than four weeks (Page 23)
- Cleaning instructions specify using mild detergent and warm water with sponges, soft cloths, or paper towels (Page 23)
- Prohibited items include cleaning waxes, concentrated detergents, bleaches, petroleum-based cleaners, paper towels, window sprays, scouring cleansers, and flammable fluids (Page 23)
- The defrost pan must be removed by reaching into a small opening at the right edge and reinstalled fully (Page 23)
- Condenser coils should be vacuumed when dusty or dirty, potentially as often as every other month (Page 23)
- The floor under the refrigerator can only be cleaned by rolling the unit out as far as the water supply line allows (Page 23)
- For short holidays, users are instructed to use up perishables, freeze other items, raise the ice maker signal arm to OFF, shut off the water supply to the ice maker, and empty the ice bin (Page 23)
- For long holidays, remove all food, turn off the water supply to the ice maker one day ahead, unplug the refrigerator, clean it thoroughly, and tape the doors open (Page 24)
- A "WARNING" box states that children may become injured or trapped if they climb on or inside a refrigerator with blocked-open doors (Page 24)
- When moving, disconnect the water line, remove all food, pack frozen items in dry ice, and tape the doors shut (Page 24)
- For power interruptions lasting more than 24 hours, options are to store food in a locker, use 32 grams of dry ice per liter of freezer space, or consume perishable food immediately (Page 24)
- A full freezer stays cold longer than a partly filled one, and meat-filled freezers stay cold longer than those with baked goods (Page 24)
- Food should be stored in air-tight and moisture-proof material to prevent odor and taste transfer (Page 25)
- Leafy vegetables should be washed, drained, and stored in a plastic bag or container in the crisper (Page 25)
- Fruit should be washed, dried, and stored in plastic bags or a crisper; berries should not be washed until ready to use (Page 25)
- Eggs should be stored in their original carton on an interior shelf (Page 25)
- Meat should be stored in its original airtight wrapping, and a chart provides storage times (Page 25)
